body: CIO of Alliance Capital's Indian MF business 1993-Aug 2003 (funds won 15+ awards); founded Helios Capital (Singapore) in 2005; Helios MF in India launched 2023-24 (its flexi-cap fund has posted strong early returns per Value Research). A Morningstar/PMS-AIF profile claims ~25% a year (219x) since 1996 vs ~12.2% (16x) for the Indian market in INR - combining Alliance and Helios records (single-source, unaudited). His 2003 departure from Alliance followed a SEBI order that was later overturned on appeal (details not re-verified here). Process edge: (1) an 'avoid list' - he excludes whole sectors with poor long-run shareholder returns or governance (PSUs, many commodities, utilities, real estate) to cut error rates; (2) sell losers early rather than average down; (3) diversified 30-40 stock portfolios in growth sectors (private financials, consumer, tech); (4) he argues fewer than 5% of stocks are worth holding long term, so 'buy and hold' alone is not enough. Mistakes: the avoid list made Helios miss the 2021-24 PSU/defence/railway rally (characterisation); he cut equity sharply in early 2020 on COVID (reported; unverified) and had to re-enter. Copyable: write your own avoid list (sectors with chronic capital destruction), set a sell rule for thesis-broken losers, and accept missing some rallies as the price of fewer blow-ups.
